facts.text: Measured 2026-11-16 on real sessions: 57 of 162 turns are short messages (under 8 content words, mostly go-aheads like 'yes, start from A+B'); only 47% of them get any recalled fact against 73-97% of longer ones, and their facts are used most (27%). Enriching a short message with the previous reply (last 200/400 or first 200 characters) doubles the facts shown (56 -> ~107) and finds no additional relevant one (3 -> 3) on a relevance set built from the same turns; on all messages it makes long ones worse (24 -> 21). ADR-020 D3 is not adopted.
facts.gist: short msgs = 35% of turns, 47% get a fact; previous-reply enrichment: 2x facts shown, 0 more relevant -> ADR-020 D3 not

facts.text: A/B 2 on 18/11 (9 scenarios incl. failed-solution cases, 2 reps, 8 Haiku subagents with 4-5 independent cases each): When/If prose 18/18 and Issue/context/Solutions 18/18 once two scorer false negatives are fixed; same length (~270-450 chars); so the issue/solutions shape is not more readable for the model, its value is structural (store fields, merge solutions, failed attempts, graph edges).
facts.gist: A/B2: When/If 18/18 = Issue/Solutions 18/18; Issue format gains are structural, not readability

facts.text: Asked on 2026-11-16 what would be truly useful to it as a model, the assistant answered from that day's work: (1) negative knowledge with its number, i.e. what was tried, failed and why, so it is not proposed again; (2) where the work stood at the last stop, which it had to pull by hand that morning; (3) procedures with proof that they worked, like the install command it found only in a client memory file; (4) an explicit 'the memory holds nothing on this' instead of silence; (5) for each fact who wrote it, when, and whether anyone disputed it. Fewer decisive facts over more recall.
facts.gist: model's own wishlist 16/11: failed attempts with numbers, last-stop state, proven procedures, explicit 'nothing known',

facts.text: Measured 2026-11-16 on 321 real showings (125 facts, 17 sessions, 55 used): among shown facts the similarity to the message does not predict use (AUC cosine 0.50, logistic fit on cosine/named/lexical/age 0.51 leaving a session out, use rate flat at 16-20% across cosine bands), so ADR-019's calibrated score is closed as measured, not adopted; the fact's own history does predict it (used in another session: 30% used again, never used elsewhere: 11%, AUC 0.66), but only as a positive signal: dropping never-used facts loses uses at the base rate.
facts.gist: 16/11: similarity does not predict use (AUC .50), per-fact history does (30% vs 11%, AUC .66), positive only; ADR-019 no

facts.text: 23/11 proposal: promotion as a bridge, not a copy. For a proven Neuron fact, find via knowledge_query the NeuRAG DOCUMENT node on the same subject and create the fact->document bridge; copy nothing. Neuron stays the single owner (supersede, disputes, use signal live only there); the bridge is a lazy pointer (one line, excerpts only on request). Copy-promotion rejected: the KB copy diverges when the fact is superseded (denormalization without trigger). Next: measure precision on the 29 stable candidates with a blind judge before any automatic birth.
facts.gist: idea: promotion as a fact->document bridge, no copy; measure precision blind first

facts.text: Pattern module data flow (user idea 19/11, shaped): confirmed hypotheses with evidence, domain frames written as text and closed investigation reports go to NeuRAG; work episodes (investigation opened/closed, predictions and outcomes as solves/failed_for, the user's judgments) go to Neuron; rejected hypotheses become tried: facts; raw rows never leave the module; the LLM reaches the data through a module tool exposed by GM that computes and returns one line; bridges link module ids, Neuron facts and NeuRAG chunks; only verified findings are promoted.
facts.gist: pattern module -> NeuRAG (confirmed, frames, reports), Neuron (episodes, predictions, tried); raw data stays; LLM via mo

facts.text: tried (on paper, 2026-11-17): flash or pulse for profile facts adds nothing: flash only takes idea/decision/fix and is for dormant facts among many, pulse is model-called, and profile facts not in the profile already compete in normal recall (35-43 showings over 209 real messages). Chosen instead: profile keeps identity and always-on reply rules; task-tied rules (commit, release, other sessions) may leave it if a replay shows they come back when the task is named.
facts.gist: flash/pulse for profile: no gain; split always-on rules vs task-tied rules, verify by replay

facts.text: tried: semantic concept naming (message words/bigrams vs concept vectors, NEURON_FACT_NAMED_SEM) on 19/11: at 0.80 worse on all three recall benches (Italian 18->17/33, noise 0.59->0.77, first off-topic fact; procedures noise 0.50->0.57; English 19->18/33), at 0.90/0.95 no gain anywhere, and the Italian replay-procedure probe stayed at rank 43-47; code reverted. Remaining option: a bilingual concept vocabulary generated once by a cheap model and matched lexically, but only after building a bench of Italian messages against English concepts.
facts.gist: tried: semantic concept naming 0.80/0.90/0.95 -> worse or no gain; reverted; next only bilingual vocab + IT/EN bench

facts.text: Rejected 24/11: linking an isolated concept to its nearest neighbour by vector. On 345 isolated live concepts the nearest cosine looked high (median 0.74) but was wrong even at the top (sed -> java at 0.90, backfill -> backup at 0.64), so no threshold separates good from bad; the concept sharing the most facts was adopted instead.
facts.gist: tried: link isolated concept to nearest vector -> wrong even at cos 0.90 (sed->java); use shared fact

facts.text: Fable needs review 24/11: needs 2, 3, 5 done, 4 parked; need 1 (what already failed) is a real gap: only 6 'tried:' decisions, and a rejected idea is recalled only with its own keywords (cos 0.78) while an Italian paraphrase scores 0.21-0.24 and an English one 0.47 against the English fact (MiniLM multilingual). Cross-lingual paraphrase recall is the root, not the tried: format. Proposed: small IT-paraphrase bench (~20 questions on existing facts), then compare bilingual concepts at write time vs multilingual-e5.
